analysis_scope.sampling_notes: The supplied checkout was described as a shallow depth-50 clone, so history should be treated as a recent-history sample. Git reports this checkout as not shallow and exposes only 14 reachable commits, all of which were inspected. The repository is small enough that every tracked file was inspected; secret values were neither sought nor read.

observed_capabilities.statement: The PyBank notebook reads dated profit-and-loss rows from a relative CSV path and calculates month count, total profit or loss, average month-to-month change, and the greatest increase and decrease.
The PyBank artifacts preserve results for 86 months, a $22,564,198 total, a -$8,311.11 average change, an August 2016 greatest increase, and a February 2014 greatest decrease.

The PyPoll notebook reads election rows from a relative CSV path, counts votes for three hard-coded candidates, calculates percentages, selects the highest-percentage candidate, and formats a text report.
The PyPoll artifacts preserve results for 369,711 votes and identify Diana DeGette as the winner with 73.812 percent of votes.

architecture.statement: The repository consists of two independent Jupyter notebook workflows, each using only Python standard-library os and csv modules, expecting an untracked CSV under a working-directory-relative Resources folder, and writing output.txt in the current working directory.
There is no shared package, reusable analysis module, application entry point, data store, or orchestration layer connecting the two workflows.

accomplishments.statement: Both analysis exercises have substantive calculation logic and committed example result files.
The committed text reports agree with the corresponding result values preserved in notebook output.
The repository's ignore rules exclude common Python build products, virtual environments, notebook checkpoints, test caches, and .env files.

gaps.statement: The README contains only the repository title and does not explain the exercises, inputs, setup, execution procedure, expected results, or limitations.
Neither required CSV dataset is tracked, so the notebooks cannot be rerun from this checkout without separately obtaining and placing the inputs.

The PyBank calculation loops over len(P), but P is never defined by any tracked notebook cell; its saved success therefore depends on hidden kernel state or a variable omitted from the committed notebook.

The PyPoll output-writing cell has no execution count or saved output, so the notebook itself does not demonstrate that this final cell ran in the committed session even though a matching output.txt is tracked.
There are no tests, dependency manifests, CI checks, or reproducible execution instructions.

risks.statement: A clean execution of PyBank is likely to fail with an undefined-name error even after the missing dataset is supplied.

Saved notebook state and committed output files can conceal source regressions because there is no clean-kernel execution or automated comparison validating that the current code reproduces the results.
PyPoll classifies every candidate other than two named candidates as Raymon Anthony Doane, so changed or expanded input data would silently produce incorrect attribution.
PyPoll stores every input column and repeatedly appends a reference to the complete candidates list while counting votes, consuming substantially more memory than direct counters require.
The latest available commit is from July 2022 and no tests, releases, issues, or operational artifacts indicate ongoing maintenance.

suggested_next_actions.statement: Treat the repository as dormant coursework unless the owner still intends to use it; any lifecycle change remains subject to owner review.
If retained as a runnable reference, replace len(P) with the intended collection, restart and execute both notebooks from clean kernels against documented inputs, and refresh the committed outputs.
Document dataset provenance and acquisition without committing restricted coursework data, then add concise usage instructions and small representative fixtures with automated result tests.
Replace PyPoll's hard-coded candidate branches and list accumulation with a dictionary-based counter so arbitrary candidates are counted correctly and efficiently.

questions: Was this repository created for a specific course or bootcamp assignment, and should that context be recorded?
Are the omitted Resources CSV files intentionally excluded because of licensing or course-distribution restrictions?
Is the repository worth repairing as a personal reference, or should it simply remain archived coursework?
What variable was P intended to reference in the PyBank notebook?

evidence.summary: Supplied metadata identifies a public repository on main with no description, no open issues or pull requests, and a latest push timestamp of 2022-07-24.
The 20-byte README contains only the heading Python---Challenge.

The complete tracked tree contains .gitignore, README.md, two notebooks, and two text outputs; no Resources datasets, manifests, tests, workflows, documentation tree, scripts, credential files, or deployment artifacts are tracked.

Python 3.8.13 notebook using os and csv to analyze Resources/budget_data.csv and write output.txt; saved results are present, but the calculation references an undefined P variable and execution counts begin 1, 6, 7, and 8.
Committed financial report records 86 months, total $22,564,198, average change -$8,311.11, and greatest increase and decrease details.

Python 3.8.13 notebook using os and csv to analyze Resources/election_data.csv, with three hard-coded candidate branches, list-based vote counting, saved console results, and an unexecuted final output-writing cell.
Committed election report records 369,711 votes, candidate totals and percentages, and Diana DeGette as winner.
Standard Python ignore rules cover build artifacts, environments, caches, notebook checkpoints, and .env files.
Fourteen available commits span 2022-03-21 through 2022-07-24 and primarily create, upload, or delete notebook-related files; the latest commit is 2b09c26.

confidence.rationale: The repository is small and every tracked artifact plus all available commits was inspected. Source, notebook state, and committed outputs clearly support the implementation and reproducibility findings, although execution could not be independently repeated because the required datasets are absent and live GitHub metadata was unavailable.

limitations: The required CSV inputs are absent, so calculations were assessed statically and from committed outputs rather than rerun.
The supplied clone was described as depth-50, so history beyond the available checkout cannot be assumed even though git reports the checkout as not shallow.
Live GitHub archival state, branches beyond fetched references, releases, and remote issue or pull-request state could not be independently verified because the GitHub API was unreachable.
The repository provides no substantive purpose statement, so coursework classification is an evidence-based inference from its structure and exercises rather than an explicit owner declaration.
